To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of nanoparticles to epoxy resins can improve the fatigue crack growth resistance of the epoxy resin by crack deflection and crack tip bridging, and that the geometrical appearance of the particles is of crucial importance for the fatigue crack growth behaviour.

the FCP behaviour can be improved significantly by the addition of nano-spherical silica or large O/K-hects, and that the geometrical appearance of the nano-particles has a huge impact on their toughening effect.
the addition of nanoparticles to the epoxy resin leads to a significant reduction in the crack growth rates, especially in the region of stable crack propagation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fatigue crack growth behaviour of epoxy nanocomposites.
the fatigue crack growth behaviour of epoxy resins with spherical and platelet-like nano-fillers.
the fatigue crack propagation behaviour of epoxy nanocomposites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spherical nano-silicas and O/K-hects with large lateral extensions and high aspect ratios are very suitable for improving the FCP behaviour of epoxy resins.
spherical nano-silicas are suitable for toughening epoxy resins at low amounts, whereas large plate-like nano-clays are more suitable at high amounts.
the FCP of epoxy nanocomposites is strongly affected by the geometry of the particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the geometrical appearance of the nanoparticles plays a crucial role for the fatigue crack growth behaviour of epoxy nanocomposites and the toughening mechanism is strongly dependent on the particle geometry.
the FCP behaviour of epoxy nanocomposites can be tuned by the geometrical properties of the nanoparticles.
the FCP of an epoxy resin is significantly improved by the addition of spherical nano-silicas and large lateral extended clay tactoids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
particle geometry has to be taken into consideration when designing nanocomposite materials for structural applications.
the FCP resistance of an epoxy resin can be improved by using a small amount of surface-modified spherical silica or K-fluorohectorites.
the FCP of epoxy resin can be improved significantly by the addition of nanoparticles with different geometrical appearances.
